chunk_map.heading: What would have caught this earlier?
Three failure modes you'll use to read
Every long session is suspect on all three
The same three checks at larger scale

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative/named-referent against the sequential-read bar. Chunk 3 line 20 "a failure outside the menu gets its own name" -- "the menu" reads as a metaphor for the three-item list, but sits in the same sentence directly after "Check the artefact against all three" so a sequential reader resolves it by immediate proximity; the harm rule 1 guards against (a referent the reader cannot place) is absent. Chunk 4 line 26 "Your session had nothing of the kind" -- "session" is named repeatedly in earlier chunks (line 5 "The session finished, hit its budget"; line 7 "caught this earlier in the session"; line 19 "As the session grows") and resolves cleanly as the file's own load-bearing recurring noun -- confirmed no "run"-as-noun survivors remain anywhere in body (grep -noE '\brun\b|\bruns\b' over lines 1-27 -> 0 hits; all 16 body-region matches for the bare string "run" sit at line 32+, inside the maintainer/backing fence, register-exempt). Chunk 1 line 6's "the send-off prompt" is a fresh named artifact, not a pronoun, and self-unpacks in the same sentence (see rule 2).

grep -inE 'the opening lecture|earlier lecture|the prework at the top' over lines 1-27 -> 0 hits. Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 6, "the send-off prompt says *rather than inventing a way forward*" -- names a real artifact by role and unpacks its claim with a direct quote in the same sentence, clearing the navigational-pointer carve-out (name by title/claim, ideally unpacked same-sentence). Not located by page position anywhere ("above", "the prompt you pasted earlier on this page"). "the same way" (chunk 4, line 25) is an in-chunk callback to the immediately preceding bullet, not cross-file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'the .* you (did|saw|caught|found)' over lines 1-27 -> 0 hits. No "the X you did/saw" construction naming a specific completed exercise beat appears anywhere in body; this file is deliberately module-free per its own maintainer Delivery-mode note, so the construction this rule polices has no instance to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'guess|predict' over lines 1-27 -> 0 hits. No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in body.

Chunk 0 is title-only (H1, no lede) -- the template's own designated title-slide shape, not a wait-state/context-dependent fragment. Chunks 1-4 each carry 2-5 multi-clause bullets with their own self-carrying claim (e.g. chunk 3's two bullets stand alone as the statistical-machine mechanism claim and the vigilance-governor claim); none is a single context-dependent bullet.

All four headers (lines 3, 9, 17, 22) match their chunk's bullets. Closest candidate: chunk 4 header "The same three checks at larger scale", lines 22-27 -- bullets describe external validation existing on two ports rather than literally re-walking each of the three failure modes against each port, but that is the chunk-3 vigilance principle applied at scale, not a contradiction; the backing block's `same-three-checks-at-scale` entry confirms the header deliberately applies the principle without claiming either port exhibited a specific mode.

chunk 1 "What would have caught this earlier?", line 7: "Not *did the task succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*. A diagnostic: you read the artefact, you find what went wrong, and for each thing you ask this one question." Verbatim instance of the banned "Not X. Not Y. Z." shape. Harm the sub-item guards against (the templated triad reading as formulaic rhetorical filler rather than a direct statement) is present here -- the same disambiguating content recasts into one sentence without losing either ruled-out reading, so the fix would not degrade the artefact, and no maintainer accept-note covers this passage. Every other rule-7 sub-item checked clean across all chunks: no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlatives (grep -inE 'one of the most|most useful' -> 0 hits); no number-plus-retraction (the exact figures in chunk 4 -- 10 hours/2.2M tokens, eleven days/about 64 agents -- carry no retraction clause, and the backing block's ronacher-ten-hour-port and sumner-bun-scale entries attest the figures are deliberately exact, kept rather than hedged); no abstraction-noun stacks ("a finite window", "the working window" are established plain technical terms, defined in-line); no empty-leg verb triplets.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast as one declarative, e.g. "The question that drives the read is diagnostic, not a verdict on task success or spec quality: what would have caught this earlier in the session?" -- drop the two standalone "Not ___" sentences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections|\bsurface\b' over body lines 1-27 -> 0 hits. Closest candidate: chunk 2 line 15 "did the rules you compounded actually reach the work?" -- reads as ordinary English (accumulated/built up over the session), the plain ambient sense of "compound," not a reference to the repo's internal /compound skill; an AE101 engineer reader has no reason to parse it as jargon. "artefact", "session", "read", "window" are this file's own defined vocabulary or ordinary engineering words, not repo/maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\*\*' over body lines 1-27 -> exactly 3 hits, all in chunk 2: **Goal drift.**, **Context rot.**, **Plausible-but-wrong.** (lines 12-14). Three named failure-mode handles on one slide fits the rule's own law/consolidation-slide exception (one handle per law); the maintainer block's Emphasis-pass note (2026-07-09, "go very lightly on the bold") confirms this exact reduction was the deliberate outcome of applying §9. No bold anywhere in chunks 0, 1, 3, 4.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a flat `curriculum/lectures/` file, the in-scope surface type per compendium frontmatter. Body is a plain run of `##` chunks under the lecture's own single M5 inclusion (`learn-from-the-test.md § Start here` per maintainer Delivery-mode note); no phase-less prose sub-section of the kind rule 10's canonical failure describes (a prework/supplementary/reference block dropped for lacking a `.phase--*`/`section.module` wrapper) -- nothing here to drop from the composed deck. Not independently re-verified against a live headless-Chrome render this session; this is a structural read, not a tool-run claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Pure lecture file (zero imperative/phase-label headers), so the mood-switch mechanism the rule protects (a rare declarative standing out against an exercise's imperative norm) has no imperative baseline to contrast against here. The rule's 2026-08-15 measurement is scoped to the 15 AE101 exercise files, not lecture headers. Of the four headers: line 17 "Every long session is suspect on all three" is a full declarative claim in the rule's intended shape; lines 9/22 are topic noun-phrases, not exercise-style imperative/phase-label; line 3 "What would have caught this earlier?" is the file's own driving diagnostic question -- the backing block's `driving-question` claim entry names this exact phrase as "the file's whole reason to exist, and deliberately a question rather than a checklist," so rewriting it into a flat claim would degrade the artefact's own stated design, not merely restyle a heading.
